label: Revision-authored AQA-style practice question (original, not an AQA question)

question.context: Original Revision practice. A (2 days) precedes parallel B (4 days) and C (3 days); D (2 days) waits for BOTH. C now increases from 3 to 5 days, while all other durations and dependencies are unchanged.
question.stem: After amending the network timings, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: A–C–D becomes critical and the project takes 9 days; B has 1 day of float.

options.label: B
options.text: A–B–D stays critical and the project still takes 8 days.

options.label: C
options.text: The project takes 11 days because B and C must happen sequentially.

options.label: D
options.text: A–C–D becomes critical at 9 days, and B still has zero float.

option_rationale: A is correct because the C route now lasts 2+5+0+2 = 9 days, and the unchanged B route lasts 8 days.
B is incorrect because increasing C to 5 days makes its branch one day longer than B.
C is incorrect because B and C remain parallel; their durations are not summed sequentially.
D is incorrect because the eight-day B route can now slip one day before delaying the nine-day project.
mark_scheme.model_answer: A. A–C–dummy–D now takes 9 days and becomes critical. A–B–D takes 8, so B has 1 day of total float.
